text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.6% today as oil prices surged on geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Eastern Europe. A deadly Saudi airport attack pushed Brent crude above $106 a barrel, while uncertainty around a U.S.-brokered energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine kept markets on edge. The stock has climbed 9% over two weeks as global oil prices have climbed—Brent is now trading at $125.44 per barrel, well above the $96 level for U.S. crude, signaling tight global supplies.

Energy companies like ConocoPhillips tend to benefit when oil prices rise, since higher crude translates to stronger margins on their production and refining operations. The ongoing Middle East tensions and questions about whether Russian energy sanctions will fully ease add to the bullish backdrop for oil prices heading into the final stretch before the midterm elections.
